content.mainTextFull: UI-001 · Verification evidenceState display primitives & shell proofThis surface renders the full state-primitive matrix, the environment-signal derivation chain with an anti-spoof probe, the role-routing matrix for all five roles plus the unauthenticated view, and the single navigation grammar registry. It is deep-linkable and allowed for every audience per the grammar. Every state rendered below is a demonstration fixture with demonstration authorities — no financial semantics and no product outcomes exist on this surface.1 · Environment signal — derivation and anti-spoofingA persistent, always-visible environment signal distinguishes sandbox from production, derived exclusively from explicit configuration (UX contract Section 10). This is the only chain that sets it:Configuration: the deployment sets the server-side variable PAYSWAP_ENV before build/start. URL parameters, user content, and client state do not participate.Validation: exact allowlist — the values sandbox and production.Fail-safe: unset or invalid resolves to sandbox. Production framing appears only when configuration explicitly says production, so sandbox execution can never read as production execution (N4).Resolution: the server root layout (src/app/layout.tsx) resolves the signal once per render and passes it to the banner as a prop.Presentation: the banner is a server component pinned to the top of every route. No control anywhere re-labels the environment.Current classification: unset-or-invalid → resolved sandboxSource: PAYSWAP_ENV — server-side build/start-time configuration. This page is a server component that re-derives the value from the same module the layout uses — there is exactly one derivation path. Raw configuration values are never echoed; only this classified summary renders.Anti-spoof probe — no attempt detectedNo environment parameter is present in this URL. The banner at the top reads the value resolved on the server from explicit configuration only.Try to spoof it: /state-primitives?env=productionAfter navigating, this probe reports the ignored attempt and the banner still reads the configured environment.2 · State primitive matrixEvery stateful rendering resolves to exactly one of six explicit display states (P4). Each primitive is visually and semantically distinct — its own icon shape, border style, tint, and label word; color never carries the distinction alone (P5, P9). Each card below is deep-linkable (for example #state-unknown), and every state shown is a demonstration fixture.SUCCEEDED — authority-reported successThe owning authority reports a terminal successful outcome; wording comes from the authority and an evidence link is mandatory (P7).SucceededThe reference operation completed successfully, as reported by the demonstration authority.Reported by: Demonstration authorityView the evidence record (demonstration)FAILED — authority-reported failureOnly an authority-reported terminal failure renders this. A failed fetch renders Unknown instead (see the availability case below).FailedThe reference operation failed, as reported by the demonstration authority.Reported by: Demonstration authorityReason: The demonstration authority reported a rejected precondition.Next actions:Inspect the evidence recordStart a new reference operation (when authorized)UNKNOWN — no authoritative answerDistinct label, distinct visual (dashed amber frame, question icon), plain language, and a reconciliation path where known — never styled or worded as success or failure (P5).UnknownThe current state of the reference operation is unknown.No authoritative answer is currently available, so the display state is Unknown. What is not yet known: whether the reference operation has completed, and with which outcome.Resolved by:The demonstration authority, as the owner of the reference operation stateRe-check:The next authoritative report, or a re-check once the owning surface shipsUnknown is not a success verdict and not a failure verdict.WAITING — with available actionsWhat is waiting, why (as reported by the owning authority), what happens next, and the available actions (P6).WaitingThe reference operation is waiting.Why: The demonstration authority reports the request is queued behind prior work. (as reported by Demonstration authority)What happens next: The authority processes the queue in order and reports the next state; the UI presents no invented timing estimates.Available actions:Inspect the evidence recordWAITING — no actions yet (explicit)When no action is available, the primitive says so explicitly — a non-terminal state never dead-ends (P6).WaitingThe reference operation is waiting.Why: The demonstration authority reports a delay, with no user input requested. (as reported by Demonstration authority)What happens next: The authority resumes processing and reports the next state.No action is available yet.IN_PROGRESS — actively processingWhat is happening, what completes it, and the reporting authority. The arc and strip are decorative motion, disabled under reduced motion — never a verdict (P4).In progressThe demonstration authority is actively processing the reference operation.What completes it: Processing completes when the authority reports a terminal state; the UI never promotes a non-terminal state to terminal.Reported by: Demonstration authorityACTION_REQUIRED — user action neededThe action, the reporting authority, and validity or consequence of inaction only where the authority provides them — this fixture provides neither.Action requiredAction needed: Confirm the reference detail so the demonstration authority can continue.Reported by: Demonstration authorityFetch failure — renders UNKNOWNRender conditions are distinct from outcomes (P4, P5): when the authoritative state cannot be retrieved, the display state is UNKNOWN — availability unknown — never a failure verdict.UnknownCurrent state of the reference state service: unknownThe authoritative state for the reference state service could not be retrieved (the retrieval request did not complete). This is an availability problem, not an outcome: it does not mean the operation failed, and it does not mean it succeeded.Resolved by:The owning authority for the reference state service, once reachableRe-check:Re-attempt retrieval; the display stays Unknown until an authoritative answer arrives.Unknown is not a success verdict and not a failure verdict.Side-by-side: outcome failure vs availability unknownThe two cases stay visually and semantically distinct: a thick left-accent solid rose frame with an octagon-X (authority-reported failure) versus a dashed amber frame with a question icon (no authoritative answer).If the authority reports failureFailedThe reference operation failed, as reported by the demonstration authority.Reported by: Demonstration authorityWhat a failed fetch rendersUnknownCurrent state of the reference state service: unknownThe authoritative state for the reference state service could not be retrieved. This is an availability problem, not an outcome: it does not mean the operation failed, and it does not mean it succeeded.Resolved by:The owning authority for the reference state service, once reachableRe-check:Re-attempt retrieval; the display stays Unknown until an authoritative answer arrives.Unknown is not a success verdict and not a failure verdict.3 · State transitions announce accessiblyState transitions on consequential outcomes are announced through a persistent polite live region (P9, P4). The demonstration below cycles a fixture sequence: the primitive re-renders and the live region announces each change.Demonstration only — a fixture sequence. Nothing is executed and no financial semantics are involved. Advance the state and observe the live region below.WaitingThe reference operation is waitingWhy: The demonstration authority reports the request is queued behind prior work (as reported by Demonstration authority)What happens next: The authority processes the queue in order and reports the next stateNo action is available yet.Live region (polite)Reference operation: waiting. The demonstration authority reports the request is queued.Advance state (1/3)Restart4 · Role-routing matrix (P8)Static proof for the five roles plus the unauthenticated viewer: each panel renders navigation through the same NavList component the live shell header and footer use. The matrix is static on purpose — the product ships no role-switching control, because role assignment is an authoritative input the UI never self-assigns, infers, or escalates. Unknown or unauthenticated visitors get least visibility.UnauthenticatedLeast visibility (P8). This is the live shell view today — UI-001 ships no identity input, so the shell never guesses a role.HomeState primitives (verification)Intent flow verificationTrack a paymentCustomerCustomer surfaces: intent creation, personal tracking and evidence, waiting/recovery, mediation and dispute views. Planned — later work items.HomeCapabilitiesProvider positions & trackingPlannedLiquidity positionsState primitives (verification)Intent flow verificationTrack a paymentOperatorOperator surfaces: read-only operational visibility, exactly as permitted by the owning protocol authorities. The rules:Primary navigation is declared only in the grammar module (src/lib/navigation.ts) and rendered only through the shared NavList component (src/components/shell/nav-list.tsx).Back/close semantics: the shell renders no ad hoc back or close controls. Back is the platform back affordance (browser history); close returns to the parent surface declared by the owning surface when it ships. Behavior is identical everywhere because no surface redefines it.Deep links: status views are deep-linkable, and direct entry re-checks the viewer role with guardSurface. A deep link never bypasses the grammar or the role gate.Role filtering: entries declare their audiences; unknown or unauthenticated viewers get least visibility (P8).Planned entries reserve routes in the grammar but stay inert (non-navigating, tagged Planned) until the owning work item ships them.Extensions to the grammar go through this module — never around it.The full registry — every entry, its reserved route, its audience gating, and its status:/HomeAvailableprimary navShell entry surface for every audience (UI-001).Visible to: Unauthenticated, Customer, Merchant, Provider, Operator, Administrator/state-primitivesState primitives (verification)Availablefooter navUI-001 verification surface: state-primitive matrix, environment derivation, role-routing matrix, grammar registry.Visible to: Unauthenticated, Customer, Merchant, Provider, Operator, Administrator/customer/intentsIntent creationPlannedprimary navCustomer surface — planned; content.mainTextFull: Merchant surfaceRole-checked: merchant onlyCurrent audience: merchantRuntime: ARRIVINGMock backing — NON-AUTHORITATIVE (presentation-only)Merchant checkoutOpen offers and quotes addressed to your merchant identity. Each offer shows the full consequences before any commitment; accepting and declining are separate explicit actions.Checkout truth is owned by: Checkout/Intent Authority (spec/architecture/v0.1). This surface presents authority-reported values only — it never computes amounts and never applies decisions itself.Open offers awaiting your explicit decision (2)Checkout quote for customer intent int_4b8a2e — EUR corridorCurrently reviewedpco_9f27c1 · you receive 246.15 EUR · valid until 2026-06-04 09:15 UTCReviewed belowCheckout quote for customer intent int_77d0f4 — high-band EUR corridorOpenpco_c4183d · you receive 7,368.75 EUR · valid until 2026-06-05 14:40 UTCReview this offerCheckout quote for customer intent int_4b8a2e — EUR corridorQuoted 2026-05-28 09:15 UTC · Valid until 2026-06-04 09:15 UTCProtocol reference pco_9f27c1 · Originating customer intent int_4b8a2eState: offered — decision requiredQuoted by authorityIn plain languageIf you accept, you commit to fulfil intent int_4b8a2e: the customer pays 250.00 EUR, you receive 246.15 EUR on the authority's settlement schedule, you keep fulfilment evidence for 90 days, and chargeback exposure stays with you.Read the full terms below before deciding. Nothing is committed until you explicitly accept.Quoted amountsQuoted by the authority — never computed on this surfaceCustomer pays250.00 EURQuoted by the Checkout/Intent Authority. This surface never recomputes it.You receive246.15 EURQuoted by the Checkout/Intent Authority, net of the protocol fee below.Protocol fee3.85 EURQuoted by the Checkout/Intent Authority as part of the quote.Terms of this quote — fully expandedEvery condition and obligation below is shown in full. Nothing decision-relevant is collapsed, summarized away, or hidden behind a control on this surface.Conditions — what constrains or changes this dealThe quoted figures hold only inside the validity windowMaterial conditionThe quote is valid until 2026-06-04 09:15 UTC. After that, the authority treats the offer as lapsed: accepting it later is refused, and the customer intent moves on without your fulfilment.Customer pays by SEPA instant transferThe customer's payment arrives from a SEPA-instant rail. If the customer's transfer fails on their side, this checkout moves to a failed payment state — your acceptance alone does not move money.Chargeback exposure stays with youMaterial conditionIf the customer later initiates a chargeback through their bank, the disputed amount is pulled back from your settlement balance before it is paid out to you. You are the party exposed to the dispute.Settlement runs on the authority's schedule, not instantlyMaterial conditionAfter the customer's payment is confirmed, your 246.15 EUR is scheduled for payout on the next settlement run. 'You receive' describes the quoted amount, not the moment it lands in your account.What you commit to if you acceptFulfil the customer's order once acceptance is acknowledgedObligation on acceptanceAccepting commits you to fulfil the order described in intent int_4b8a2e. The authority records your acceptance and the customer relies on it.Keep fulfilment evidence for 90 daysObligation on acceptanceYou must retain proof of fulfilment (tracking, receipt, or handover record) for 90 days after acceptance, and present it if the checkout is disputed.Refunds go through the protocol, not around itObligation on acceptanceIf you need to give money back to this customer, you request the refund through the protocol so the ledger stays consistent. Off-ledger refunds leave you exposed with no authority record.Action requiredAction needed: Decide this checkout explicitly: accept the offer or decline it. No action happens until you choose one.Reported by: mock-checkout-authority (presentation-only stand-in) standing in for the Checkout/Intent Authority (spec/architecture/v0.1)Validity: This offer is valid until 2026-06-04 09:15 UTC (authority-quoted deadline).If no action is taken: If you neither accept nor decline before the offer lapses, the customer intent moves on without your fulfilment, the quote expires, and a later acceptance is refused.Your decisionAccept and decline are two separate, single-intent actions. Neither is pre-selected, and no action is taken until you explicitly choose one.While the runtime is ARRIVING, decisions are routed through the simulated protocol authorization path of the NON-AUTHORITATIVE mock.Accept offerDecline offerTwo separate single-intent actions: accepting commits you to the obligations of this offer; declining records your refusal. Neither is pre-selected; each asks for its own confirmation.Evidence:Offer quote receipt (cko_live_offer_001)Merchant checkout surface (UI-003) · checkout truth owned by Checkout/Intent Authority (spec/architecture/v0.1)Checkout flow verification harness

content.mainTextFull: UI-001 · Product foundationPaySwap application shellEvery product surface mounts into this shell. Select a chip to see the primitive and its mandatory content.SucceededFailedUnknownWaitingIn progressAction requiredWhat the shell providesOne navigation grammarBack/close semantics, primary navigation, and deep linking are defined once in src/lib/navigation.ts and consumed by every surface. Surfaces never invent local navigation (P1).Six explicit display statesSucceeded, failed, unknown, waiting, in progress, and action required render as distinct primitives with mandatory content. Unknown is never failure; a failed fetch renders unknown, not failed (P4, P5).View the state-primitive matrixEnvironment signalThis session runs in the sandbox environment. The signal derives only from explicit build-time configuration (PAYSWAP_ENV — server-side build/start-time configuration); URL parameters, user content, and client state cannot set it, and no control re-labels it (Section 10, N4).Role-scoped navigationEntries for customer, merchant, provider, operator, and administrator are declared in the grammar. Unauthenticated visitors get least visibility, and the UI never self-assigns or escalates roles — role truth is an authoritative input (P8).Current viewEnvironmentSandbox — configuration classified as unset-or-invalid; anything other than an explicit production value resolves fail-safe to sandbox.ViewerUnauthenticated — least visibility (P8). No identity input exists in UI-001, so the shell never guesses a role.Visible navigationPrimary: Home. Footer: State primitives (verification), Intent flow verification, Track a payment.Shared breakpoints (P10)sm 640 · md 768 · lg 1024 · xl 1280 · 2xl 1536 — defined once in the grammar. Touch targets are 44px; no layout scrolls horizontally.Planned role entries are inert and tagged until their owning work items ship them. The role-routing matrix on the verification surface renders all five role views plus the unauthenticated view as static proof — the product contains no role-switching control, because role assignment is an authoritative input the UI never self-assigns (P8).

content.mainTextFull: Payswap · provider surfaceViewing as providerHomeLiquidity positionsRead-only visibility of your own liquidity, credit, and queued positions. Truth on this surface is owned by its protocol authorities: the Liquidity Authority (liquidity positions and queued positions) and the Credit Authority (credit positions), per spec/architecture/v0.1 liquidity-credit-queues.md. This surface presents their quotes; it never computes, estimates, interpolates, or caches a value as truth.Authority binding: ARRIVING (record LQ-012)The Liquidity Authority and the Credit Authority bindings arrive at runtime (ARRIVING). Until then every value on these surfaces comes from the presentation-only mock and is not authoritative. Provenance labels still name the authority that owns each value at runtime.Headline positionsRead-only summary, reported by the owning authorities. The signal derives only from explicit build-time configuration (PAYSWAP_ENV — server-side build/start-time configuration); URL parameters, user content, and client state cannot set it, and no control re-labels it (Section 10, N4).Role-scoped navigationEntries for customer, merchant, provider, operator, and administrator are declared in the grammar. content.mainTextFull: Payswap · operator surfaceViewing as operatorHomeOversightRead-only visibility of the aggregates the owning authorities permit to oversight. Truth on this surface is owned by its protocol authorities: the Liquidity Authority and the Credit Authority, per spec/architecture/v0.1 liquidity-credit-queues.md. Every value below is an authority-quoted aggregate — this surface never sums, filters, derives, or caches a value as truth.Authority binding: ARRIVING (record LQ-012)The Liquidity Authority and the Credit Authority bindings arrive at runtime (ARRIVING). Until then every value on these surfaces comes from the presentation-only mock and is not authoritative. Provenance labels still name the authority that owns each value at runtime.Oversight scopeOversight permission covers authority-quoted aggregates only. Provider-identifying positions and per-provider detail are not visible on this surface.Permitted aggregatesHeadline aggregates first; each aggregate's provenance is stated with the value. content.mainTextHead: Track a paymentEnter the reference you were given — from the payer, the merchant, or support. The current state, the plain-language history, and the complete proof trail for that reference are then shown, for viewers aut
content.mainTextFull: Track a paymentEnter the reference you were given — from the payer, the merchant, or support. The current state, the plain-language history, and the complete proof trail for that reference are then shown, for viewers authorized to see them. This surface tracks by reference only: it never lists payments, and it shows no reference you did not look up.Reference lookupThe lookup itself runs server-side; the reference is resolved against the tracking authority, which decides what your role may see.Payment or settlement referenceLook up referenceReferences are not case-sensitive. What you can see for a reference depends on the role you are viewing as.You are viewing asunauthenticatedDeep links to a reference reproduce the full status view, and are role-checked on direct entry: the viewer role is resolved server-side before anything renders.If your role is not authorized for a reference, the view says so explicitly and shows nothing about its state, history, or evidence.Every tracked state is explicitThere is no ambiguous “pending” anywhere on this surface. A tracked outcome is always in exactly one of six states:SUCCEEDEDThe outcome completed. The authority reports it, with the proof trail behind it.FAILEDThe outcome did not complete. The reason and the next actions are reported.IN_PROGRESSSomething is happening right now. The page says what is happening and what completes it.WAITINGThe outcome is waiting. The page always says why, what happens next, and which actions are available to you — or explicitly that none are available yet.UNKNOWNThe authority has not answered. The page says visibly that it is unknown, who resolves it, and what triggers a re-check.ACTION_REQUIREDSomeone must act. The page says what action, by when, and what happens if nothing is done.What this surface does not doIt does not decide outcomes, compute amounts, or produce evidence. States, histories, and proof records are answered by the authorities that own them and are only presented here. Evidence that has not been answered renders as unknown — never as a substitute.Non-authoritative presentationBacked by a presentation-only mock while the live tracking adapter is ARRIVING (runtime ARRIVING). Authority owner: the Intent Authority (tracked consequential states, plain-language history) and the Evidence Authority (proof-trail records) (spec/architecture/v0.1).

Recorded verbatim and shared with the authority and the other party.Evidence attachment referencesAdd referenceEvidence labelEvidence linkA reference is complete when it has both a label and a link. Evidence links should point at authority-backed surfaces (for example the swap's tracking record).Review and initiate this disputeOpens an inline confirmation restating the grounds and consequences. Nothing is opened with the authority until you confirm.

content.mainTextFull: UI-001 · Product foundationPaySwap application shellEvery product surface mounts into this shell. It provides one navigation grammar, six explicit display states, a persistent environment signal, and role-scoped navigation — and it deliberately carries zero financial semantics: no balances, no settlement or finality wording, no protocol states.Open the verification surfaceDisplay state vocabularyEvery stateful rendering resolves to exactly one explicit display state (P4) — no ambiguous pending. Select a chip to see the primitive and its mandatory content.SucceededFailedUnknownWaitingIn progressAction requiredWhat the shell providesOne navigation grammarBack/close semantics, primary navigation, and deep linking are defined once in src/lib/navigation.ts and consumed by every surface. Surfaces never invent local navigation (P1).Six explicit display statesSucceeded, failed, unknown, waiting, in progress, and action required render as distinct primitives with mandatory content. Unknown is never failure; a failed fetch renders unknown, not failed (P4, P5).View the state-primitive matrixEnvironment signalThis session runs in the sandbox environment. The signal derives only from explicit build-time configuration (PAYSWAP_ENV — server-side build/start-time configuration); URL parameters, user content, and client state cannot set it, and no control re-labels it (Section 10, N4).Role-scoped navigationEntries for customer, merchant, provider, operator, and administrator are declared in the grammar. Unauthenticated visitors get least visibility, and the UI never self-assigns or escalates roles — role truth is an authoritative input (P8).Current viewEnvironmentSandbox — configuration classified as unset-or-invalid; anything other than an explicit production value resolves fail-safe to sandbox.ViewerUnauthenticated — least visibility (P8). No identity input exists in UI-001, so the shell never guesses a role.Visible navigationPrimary: Home. Footer: State primitives (verification), Intent flow verification, Track a payment.Shared breakpoints (P10)sm 640 · md 768 · lg 1024 · xl 1280 · 2xl 1536 — defined once in the grammar. Touch targets are 44px; no layout scrolls horizontally.Planned role entries are inert and tagged until their owning work items ship them. The role-routing matrix on the verification surface renders all five role views plus the unauthenticated view as static proof — the product contains no role-switching control, because role assignment is an authoritative input the UI never self-assigns (P8).

content.mainTextHead: UI-001 · Product foundationPaySwap application shellEvery product surface mounts into this shell. It provides one navigation grammar, six explicit display states, a persistent environment signal, and role-scoped navigati
content.mainTextFull: UI-001 · Product foundationPaySwap application shellEvery product surface mounts into this shell. It provides one navigation grammar, six explicit display states, a persistent environment signal, and role-scoped navigation — and it deliberately carries zero financial semantics: no balances, no settlement or finality wording, no protocol states.Open the verification surfaceDisplay state vocabularyEvery stateful rendering resolves to exactly one explicit display state (P4) — no ambiguous pending. Select a chip to see the primitive and its mandatory content.SucceededFailedUnknownWaitingIn progressAction requiredWhat the shell providesOne navigation grammarBack/close semantics, primary navigation, and deep linking are defined once in src/lib/navigation.ts and consumed by every surface. Surfaces never invent local navigation (P1).Six explicit display statesSucceeded, failed, unknown, waiting, in progress, and action required render as distinct primitives with mandatory content. Unknown is never failure; a failed fetch renders unknown, not failed (P4, P5).View the state-primitive matrixEnvironment signalThis session runs in the sandbox environment. The signal derives only from explicit build-time configuration (PAYSWAP_ENV — server-side build/start-time configuration); URL parameters, user content, and client state cannot set it, and no control re-labels it (Section 10, N4).Role-scoped navigationEntries for customer, merchant, provider, operator, and administrator are declared in the grammar. Unauthenticated visitors get least visibility, and the UI never self-assigns or escalates roles — role truth is an authoritative input (P8).Current viewEnvironmentSandbox — configuration classified as unset-or-invalid; anything other than an explicit production value resolves fail-safe to sandbox.ViewerUnauthenticated — least visibility (P8). No identity input exists in UI-001, so the shell never guesses a role.Visible navigationPrimary: Home. Footer: State primitives (verification), Intent flow verification, Track a payment.Shared breakpoints (P10)sm 640 · md 768 · lg 1024 · xl 1280 · 2xl 1536 — defined once in the grammar. Touch targets are 44px; no layout scrolls horizontally.Planned role entries are inert and tagged until their owning work items ship them. The role-routing matrix on the verification surface renders all five role views plus the unauthenticated view as static proof — the product contains no role-switching control, because role assignment is an authoritative input the UI never self-assigns (P8).

This is an availability problem, not an outcome: it does not mean the operation failed, and it does not mean it succeeded.Resolved by:The owning authority for The authoritative liquidity, credit, and queue implementation, once reachableRe-check:Re-attempt retrieval; the display stays Unknown until an authoritative answer arrives.Unknown is not a success verdict and not a failure verdict.Owners of truth: the Liquidity Authority (liquidity positions, queued positions) and the Credit Authority (credit positions).No UI-side computation: every monetary value is an authority-quoted string (or an explicit authority-UNKNOWN); available is quoted in its own right, never balance minus reserved; oversight aggregates are quoted, never summed.UNKNOWN contract: indeterminate values render UNKNOWN with their reconciliation path — never zero, empty, failed, or a definitive value.At ARRIVING: the authoritative implementation binds behind the port accessor; the surfaces, the state mapping, and the mapping records stay exactly as they are.Mapping record for this state: LQ-012 (authority-binding.arriving).2 · Role-visibility matrix (P8)Only roles permitted by the owning authorities see each surface; every other audience is redirected home by requireRoleSurface. Demonstration data below is sandbox mock data, presentation-only and NON-AUTHORITATIVE (runtime ARRIVING).Adapter boundaryRole visibilityUNKNOWN sourcesPosition matrixProvenance wordingResponsive 390px1 · Adapter boundary reportWhat is authoritative here (nothing, yet), who owns the truth, and what the boundary guarantees.Boundary contractsrc/lib/protocol/liquidity-port.ts declares the surface's data needs and the port accessor. Its only backing today is src/lib/protocol/mock-liquidity-authority.ts — explicitly NON-AUTHORITATIVE, presentation-only, sandbox data only.UnknownCurrent state of The authoritative liquidity, credit, and queue implementation: unknownThe authoritative state for The authoritative liquidity, credit, and queue implementation could not be retrieved (The Liquidity Authority and the Credit Authority bindings arrive at runtime (ARRIVING), per spec/architecture/v0.1 liquidity-credit-queues.md. Until then every value on these surfaces comes from the presentation-only mock and is not authoritative.). This is an availability problem, not an outcome: it does not mean the operation failed, and it does not mean it succeeded.Resolved by:The owning authority for The authoritative liquidity, credit, and queue implementation, once reachableRe-check:Re-attempt retrieval; the display stays Unknown until an authoritative answer arrives.Unknown is not a success verdict and not a failure verdict.Owners of truth: the Liquidity Authority (liquidity positions, queued positions) and the Credit Authority (credit positions).No UI-side computation: every monetary value is an authority-quoted string (or an explicit authority-UNKNOWN); available is quoted in its own right, never balance minus reserved; oversight aggregates are quoted, never summed.UNKNOWN contract: indeterminate values render UNKNOWN with their reconciliation path — never zero, empty, failed, or a definitive value.At ARRIVING: the authoritative implementation binds behind the port accessor; the surfaces, the state mapping, and the mapping records stay exactly as they are.Mapping record for this state: LQ-012 (authority-binding.arriving).2 · Role-visibility matrix (P8)Only roles permitted by the owning authorities see each surface; every other audience is redirected home by requireRoleSurface. Deep links are role-checked. The port re-checks permission per query (defense in depth). This matrix shows statuses only — never data.Switch the simulated audiencePOST /api/shell/audience (cookie-backed), then router.refresh(). NOT AUTHORIZED reveals no state, history, or evidence.AudiencePWS-9QM2payment intent · customer, merchant, operator, administratorPWS-7F3Kpayment intent · customer, merchant, operator, administratorPWS-6KLPpayment intent · customer, merchant, operator, administratorSTL-4419settlement · merchant, provider, operator, administratorPWS-0000unknown reference · matches nothingunauthenticatedNOT AUTHORIZEDNOT AUTHORIZEDNOT AUTHORIZEDNOT AUTHORIZEDNOT FOUNDcustomerSUCCEEDEDWAITINGUNKNOWNNOT AUTHORIZEDNOT FOUNDmerchantSUCCEEDEDWAITINGUNKNOWNWAITINGNOT FOUNDproviderNOT AUTHORIZEDNOT AUTHORIZEDNOT AUTHORIZEDWAITINGNOT FOUNDoperatorSUCCEEDEDWAITINGUNKNOWNWAITINGNOT FOUNDadministratorSUCCEEDEDWAITINGUNKNOWNWAITINGNOT FOUNDAudience visibility shown per column header is a presentation choice of the mock session records; the real per-reference authorization is owned by the authorities behind the port.
